rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥīn means an unspecified span of time, potentially short or long; the Qur’an uses it in both senses.
rows.anchor: في كلام العرب وفي هذه الآية الوقت من الزمن غير محدود يقع للقليل والكثير

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He takes ḥīn here to mean seven years.
rows.anchor: يراد به سبعة أعوام، وقيل: بل يراد بذلك سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the period as one year; the author relates these durations to what was disclosed during Joseph’s imprisonment.
rows.anchor: وهذا بحسب ما كشف الغيب في سجن يوسف

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar heard a Hudhayli reading عتى حين and wrote Ibn Masud to teach people in Quraysh Arabic rather than Hudhayl’s dialect.
rows.anchor: بلغة قريش، فبها أقرئ الناس، ولا تقرئهم بلغة هذيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas counts three slips by Joseph: the episode with her, asking the cupbearer to remember him, and accusing the brothers of theft, which prompted the reply about Benjamin.
rows.anchor: عثر يوسف عليه السلام ثلاث عثرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two prisoners entered with Joseph either at the same time or separately; مع does not settle the timing.
rows.anchor: تحتمل أن تكون باقتران وقت الدخول، وأن لا تكون بل دخلوا أفذاذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two young men reportedly served the great king al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan: one was his baker and the other his cupbearer.
rows.anchor: الريان- أحدهما: خبازه، والآخر: ساقيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatā means a young man, but can also refer to an enslaved person or a free servant; the two may fit all these senses.
rows.anchor: قد تقع اللفظة على المملوك وعلى الخادم الحر

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the king suspected the baker of trying to poison him and imprisoned both men because the cupbearer agreed.
rows.anchor: الخابز منهما أراد سمه، ووافقه على ذلك الساقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph won the prisoners’ affection through his speech and virtue, comforting the sad, visiting the ill, helping the poor, and urging good.
rows.anchor: وكان يسلي حزينهم ويعود مريضهم ويسأل لفقيرهم ويندبهم إلى الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the prison keeper offered Joseph his choice of rooms, Joseph asked him not to love him, recalling the harm that followed his aunt’s, father’s, and the governor’s wife’s affection.
rows.anchor: لا تحبني يرحمك الله، فلقد أدخلت علي المحبة مضرات

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says the two prisoners staged the dreams to test Joseph’s interpretation skill.
rows.anchor: فروي عن ابن مسعود أن الفتيين استعملا هاتين المنامتين ليجرباه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the two prisoners really saw the dreams and wanted to ask Joseph about them.
rows.anchor: عم مجاهد أنهما رأيا ذلك حقيقة، فأرادا سؤاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One prisoner, reportedly named Banu, dreamed of a vine with three branches and bunches of grapes that he pressed for the king.
rows.anchor: فكنت أعصرها وأسقي الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other, reportedly named Majlath, dreamed he carried three baskets of bread on his head as birds ate from the top.
rows.anchor: وعلى رأسي ثلاث سلال فيها خبز، والطير تأكل من أعلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the grape is called wine by what it will become; others say this is the language of Oman’s Azd.
rows.anchor: قيل: إنه سمى العنب خمرا بالمئال

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi recounts an Arab carrying grapes who answered that he was carrying wine, meaning grapes.
rows.anchor: ما تحمل؟ قال: خمرا، أراد العنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubay ibn Kaʿb and Ibn Masud read the dream as pressing grapes rather than wine.
rows.anchor: في قراءة أبي بن كعب وعبد الله بن مسعود «إني أراني أعصر عنبا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can describe wine as pressed, since pressing is done for its sake.
rows.anchor: العصر لها ومن أجلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bread may have been tharīd; Ibn Masud’s codex explicitly says tharīd above the dreamer’s head.
rows.anchor: فوق رأسي ثريدا تأكل الطير منه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority understand the prisoners’ praise to mean that Joseph was excellent in knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور: يريدان في العلم

rows.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Qatada understand the praise as Joseph’s kind conduct and good treatment of fellow prisoners.
rows.anchor: من المحسنين في جريه مع أهل السجن وإجماله معهم

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says they meant Joseph had done them a personal kindness by interpreting their dreams.
rows.anchor: ونحا إليه ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them companions of the prison can refer to their residence there or to their companionship with Joseph inside it.
rows.anchor: على أن نسبهما بصحبتهما للسجن من حيث سكناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph makes a gentle, gradual argument by contrasting many divided masters with the One who is both singular and overpowering.
rows.anchor: تلطف حسن وأخذ بيسير الحجة قبل كثيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an ignorant audience, begin with a modest proof they can accept and then lead them step by step; confronting them with the whole doctrine at once may provoke rejection.
rows.anchor: فإذا قبلها لزمته عنها درجة أخرى فوقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s example also addresses people who serve worldly rulers and pin their hopes on them as though they were rival masters.
rows.anchor: وقد ابتلي بأرباب متفرقين من يخدم أبناء الدنيا ويؤملهم

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
rows.claim: Some theologians take the names to stand for the named idols themselves.
rows.anchor: ذهب بعض المتكلمين إلى أنه أوقع في هذه الآية الأسماء على المسميات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, the word name can function as self, essence, or entity, so this reading can make sense without equating name with naming.
rows.anchor: قد يجري في اللغة مجرى النفس والذات والعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse means idol names such as al-Lat and al-ʿUzza, it could mean named entities with an omitted noun understood.
rows.anchor: وحذف المضاف وأقام المضاف إليه مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred sense is that the idols have no real divinity: worship is attached only to the names people assigned them, while the objects are merely stone and wood.
rows.anchor: ما تعبدون من دونه ألوهية ولا لكم تعلق بإله إلا بحسب أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This interpretation exposes the error in claiming that a name is always identical to the thing named.
rows.anchor: إن الاسم هو المسمى في كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If names means the idols themselves, the second object of سميتم is omitted and understood as gods; on the preferred reading the pronoun refers to the assigned names.
rows.anchor: ومفعول «سميتم» الثاني محذوف، تقديره: آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word سلطان means proof or authoritative evidence.
rows.anchor: وال سلطان الحجة، وقوله: إن الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that judgment belongs to God denies that idols control decrees, destinies, or provision; it may also reject the people’s unauthorized choice of gods.
rows.anchor: ليس لأصنامكم التي سميتموها آلهة من الحكم والأقدار والأرزاق شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qayyim means upright, and most people fail to know because ignorance and disbelief dominate them.
rows.anchor: المستقيم. وأكثر الناس لا يعلمون لجهالتهم وغلبة الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph reportedly told Banu he would return to his former position serving the king, and Majlath would be crucified, after three days.
rows.anchor: أما أنت فتعود إلى مرتبتك وسقاية ربك، وقال لمجلث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says both prisoners denied having seen dreams and said they had invented them to test Joseph; another says only the man sentenced to crucifixion denied it, while a third says they saw them but later denied it.
rows.anchor: ما رأينا شيئا وإنما تحالمنا لنجربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read يسقي from saqā and others from asqā, two verbs with the same meaning; ʿIkrima and al-Jaḥdari read the passive form, meaning he will be given wine to drink.
rows.anchor: بضم الياء وفتح القاف أي ما يرويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph reports knowledge of the unseen granted by God and says the matter has already been decreed.
rows.anchor: عن غيب علمه من قبل الله تعالى: إن الأمر قد قضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ẓanna can mean certainty, since Joseph had said the outcome was settled, though it had not yet happened.
rows.anchor: بمعنى اليقين، لأن ما تقدم من قوله: قضي الأمر يلزم ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes ẓanna in its ordinary sense because dream interpretation remains conjectural.
rows.anchor: على بابه لأن عبارة الرؤيا ظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Qatada’s reading requires taking Joseph’s قضي الأمر to mean only that his interpretation was finished, not that the future was divinely settled.
rows.anchor: ولا يترتب قول قتادة إلا بأن يكون معنى قوله قضي الأمر أي قضي كلامي وقلت ما عندي وتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical reading makes the man who was promised release the subject of ظن: joy elevated him to expect rescue.
rows.anchor: أن يكون ظن مسندا إلى الذي قيل له: إنه يسقي ربه خمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks the king’s cupbearer to remember him by reporting his knowledge and standing, his wrongful imprisonment, or both.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يريد أن يذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes the pronoun in أنساه refer to Joseph: he forgot to appeal to God and relied on a human; reports say Gabriel reproached him and this prolonged the prison term.
rows.anchor: نسي في ذلك الوقت أن يشتكي إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported divine address says Joseph took an intermediary besides God and would therefore remain imprisoned longer.
rows.anchor: يا يوسف اتخذت من دوني وكيلا لأطيلن حبسك

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq makes the pronoun refer to the cupbearer, who forgot to mention Joseph to his master; رب then means the king.
rows.anchor: أي نسي ذكر يوسف عند ربه، فأضاف الذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The most common definition of biḍʿ is three to ten; Ibn Abbas’s definition informs Malik’s rule in claims and oaths.
rows.anchor: فالأكثر على أنه من الثلاثة إلى العشرة، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says biḍʿ is below a full decade and below half of one, ranging from one to four.
rows.anchor: لا يبلغ العقد ولا نصف العقد، وإنما هو من الواحد إلى الأربعة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash gives biḍʿ the range one to ten.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش «البضع» من الواحد إلى العشرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada defines biḍʿ as three to nine, supported by a prophetic explanation to Abu Bakr about the Romans’ victory over Persia.
rows.anchor: من الثلاثة إلى التسعة، ويقوي هذا ما روي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid narrows biḍʿ to three through seven.
rows.anchor: من الثلاثة إلى السبعة، قال الفراء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says biḍʿ is used with tens but not with hundreds or thousands.
rows.anchor: لا يذكر مع مائة ولا مع ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say Joseph had already served five years, then received seven years for asking the cupbearer to remember him; another report gives two additional years.
rows.anchor: فكانت مدة سجنه اثنتي عشرة سنة، وقيل: عوقب ببقاء سنتين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan attributes to the Prophet the saying that Joseph would not have remained imprisoned so long if not for his word; Hasan wept and warned that people turn to others when trouble comes.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لولا كلمته ما لبث في السجن طول ما لبث»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king says he sees the dream while describing a past dream, using the present because the vision is being contemplated now.
rows.anchor: إني أرى في المنام أني أذبحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report adds that seven thin cows emerged after the fat cows from a river and ate them, then disappeared inside their bellies.
rows.anchor: فرأيتها أكلت تلك السمان حتى حصلت في بطونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIjāf describes cows that have reached the extreme of emaciation.
rows.anchor: التي بلغت غاية الهزال، ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet’s description of Meccan men as emaciated witnesses this meaning of عجاف.
rows.anchor: ورجال مكة مسنتون عجاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ in pronouncing the two hamzas of أفتوني; another group pronounces an intervening alif as wāw.
rows.anchor: بأن لفظت بألف «أفتوني» واوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in للرؤيا links and emphasizes the fronted object; dream interpretation is named for crossing a river from one bank to another, as the interpreter reaches the dream’s endpoint.
rows.anchor: من عبر النهر، وهو تجاوزه من شط إلى شط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḍighth is a bundle larger than a handful but smaller than a sheaf, sometimes one plant and sometimes a mixture.
rows.anchor: أقل من الحزمة وأكثر من القبضة من النبات والعشب ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mixed dreams are compared to a mixed bundle of plants; the verse about Job taking a bundle is another use of ḍighth.
rows.anchor: وخذ بيدك ضغثا [ص: 44] وروي أنه أخذ عثكالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The courtiers dismiss the king’s vision as muddled dreams caused by sleep and deny expertise in confused dreams, not in true visions generally.
rows.anchor: فإنما نفوا عن أنفسهم عبر الأحلام لا عبر الرؤيا على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet distinguishes a vision from God from a disturbing dream from Satan.
rows.anchor: الرؤيا من الله والحلم من الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet told a person whose dream involved his head being cut off and restored not to recount it when Satan plays with someone in sleep.
rows.anchor: إذا لعب الشيطان بأحدكم في النوم فلا يحدث بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muddled dreams and inner thoughts are disregarded; a true vision is what can be interpreted and investigated.
rows.anchor: فالأحلام وحدثان النفس ملغاة، والرؤيا هي التي تعبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in بعالمين adds emphasis, while ب in بتأويل marks the object and depends on بعالمين.
rows.anchor: في قولهم: بتأويل للتعدية وهي متعلقة بقولهم بعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dreaming in sleep is recognized by Islamic law; the Prophet says good visions are from God and upsetting dreams from Satan, and prescribes spitting left and seeking refuge.
rows.anchor: فليتفل على يساره ثلاث مرات وليقل: أعوذ بالله من شر ما رأيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thoughts generated while awake receive no interpretive weight.
rows.anchor: وما كان عن حديث النفس في اليقظة فإنه لا يلتفت إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surviving cupbearer remembered Joseph after hearing the king and courtiers discuss the dream.
rows.anchor: تذكر يوسف وعلمه بتأويل الأحلام والرؤى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iddakkara derives from idtakara, with consonant changes and assimilation; other Arabic forms and Qur’anic readings show the same alternation.
rows.anchor: من الذكر، قلبت التاء دالا وأدغم الأول في الثاني

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read baʿda ummah as after a period of time.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس: «بعد أمة»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others read ummah as forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وجماعة «بعد أمة» وهو النسيان

rows.speaker: مجاهد وشبل بن عزرة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Shibl ibn ʿUzra read ummah with a still mīm, as a verbal noun meaning forgetting.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وشبل بن عزرة «بعد أمه» بسكون الميم

rows.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
rows.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqayli reads immah as a blessing and interprets the phrase as God’s favor in bringing Joseph near release and honor.
rows.anchor: بعد نعمة أنعمها الله على يوسف في تقريب إطلاقه وعزته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb remembered strengthens the reading that the forgotten person in the earlier story was Joseph and the forgetter was the cupbearer, though the issue remains open.
rows.anchor: عائد على الساقي، والأمر محتمل

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read أنا أنبئكم, while al-Hasan and Ubay’s codex have أنا آتيكم.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن: «أنا آتيكم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-arsilūn is a request for permission to go; Ibn Abbas says the prison was outside the king’s city, while others place it within the city.
rows.anchor: كان السجن في غير مدينة الملك- قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that people in his own day identify Joseph’s prison beside the Nile, eight miles from Fustat.
rows.anchor: ويرسم الناس اليوم سجن يوسف في موضع على النيل بينه وبين الفسطاط ثمانية أميال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer calls Joseph ṣiddīq because his honesty had been tested repeatedly; the word is an intensive form of truthful.
rows.anchor: من حيث كان جرب صدقه في غير شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr was called ṣiddīq because he affirmed others, and believers are also called truthful in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: والذين آمنوا بالله ورسله أولئك هم الصديقون

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash reports that Gabriel visited Joseph in prison with news of God’s favor and that the king’s dream would bring his release.
rows.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام دخل على يوسف في السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report gives extra details of the king’s dream: fat cows emerged from a river, were eaten by thin cows, and green ears were covered by dry ones.
rows.anchor: وقد التفت بها سبع يابسات، حتى كانت تغطي خضرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request that people may know can mean learning the dream’s interpretation and easing the king’s and people’s worry.
rows.anchor: هذه الرؤيا، فيزول هم الملك لذلك وهم الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they would recognize Joseph’s learning and excellence, leading to his release.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يعلمون مكانتك من العلم وكنه فضلك فيكون ذلك سببا لتخلصك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s answer combines symbolic interpretation, practical advice to store grain in its ear, and information about the eighth year, which Qatada counts as knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: تضمن هذا الكلام من يوسف عليه السلام ثلاثة أنواع من القول

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada treats Joseph’s prediction about the eighth year as disclosure of the unseen.
rows.anchor: الإعلام بالغيب في أمر العام الثامن، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the prediction may be ordinary dream interpretation: the end of drought implies a rich harvest, and the river represents time, just as cows represent years.
rows.anchor: إذ هو أشبه شيء به فجاءت البقرات مثالا للسنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daʾban means persistently, following the customary pattern of farming; Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse illustrates it.
rows.anchor: ملازمة لعادتكم في الزراعة، ومنه قول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven readers generally give daʾban a silent hamza; ʿAsim opens it, and Abu ʿAmr eases the hamza in connected recitation.
rows.anchor: وأبو عمرو يسهل الهمزة عند درج القراءة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad makes daʾban the object of تزرعون, understood to imply that they work diligently.
rows.anchor: عند أبي العباس المبرد، إذ في قوله تزرعون تدأبون

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh instead supplies an implicit verb from the same root to govern the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وسيبويه يرى نصب هذا كله بفعل مضمر من لفظ المصدر يدل عليه هذا الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Storing grain in the ear is a wise response to Egyptian grain that will not keep for two years otherwise; eat the oldest store first and keep the remainder for famine.
rows.anchor: فإن الحبة إذا بقيت في خبائها انحفظت والمعنى: اتركوا الزرع في السنبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s storage plan lets successive harvests carry the population through the seven drought years, using even the scant produce obtained during famine.
rows.anchor: ويؤكل الأقدم فالأقدم فإذا جاءت السنون الجدبة تقوت الناس الأقدم فالأقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed for Quraysh to suffer seven years like Joseph’s famine; the hardship began but ended before seven years.
rows.anchor: اللهم أعني عليهم بسبع كسبع يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the king put Joseph in charge of food supplies for the coming years after hearing his plan.
rows.anchor: قد أسندت إليك تولي هذا الأمر في الأطعمة هذه السنين المقبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse makes the years themselves eat by metonymy, since people eat during those years; drought may also be described as consuming and drying vegetation.
rows.anchor: إلى السنين اتساعا من حيث يؤكل فيها كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic descriptions of famine say that a year stripped everything bare, dried stars, meat, and bone.
rows.anchor: فأصابتهم سنة حصت كل شيء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Taḥṣinūn means to guard and store up, from the word for a protected fortress.
rows.anchor: تحرزون وتخزنون، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والجمهور
rows.claim: The phrase يغاث الناس may derive from rain, meaning people will receive rain.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس ومجاهد وجمهور المفسرين، أي يمطرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it can mean God relieves them; ghawth is relief.
rows.anchor: من أغاثهم الله، أذا فرج عنهم، ومنه الغوث وهو الفرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, and ʿAsim read yaʿṣirūn; Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the address form taʿṣirūn.
rows.anchor: بفتح الياء وكسر الصاد، وقرأ حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most interpreters take the verb as pressing produce such as olives, grapes, sugar cane, sesame, and radish; milking is also pressing.
rows.anchor: هي من عصر النباتات كالزيتون والعنب والقصب والسمسم والفجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that people could not press anything during the drought years.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهم لم يعصروا شيئا مدة الجدب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وغيره
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and others derive the verb from ʿaṣra, refuge or relief, rather than pressing.
rows.anchor: ذلك مأخوذ من العصرة والعصر وهو الملجأ ومنه قول أبي زبيد في عثمان رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetry by Abu Zubayd, ʿAdi ibn Zayd, Ibn Muqbil, and Labid uses ʿaṣr and related forms to mean refuge or a place to take shelter.
rows.anchor: فالآية على معنى ينجون بالعصرة

rows.speaker: الأعرج وعيسى وجعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: These readers use the passive yuʿṣarūn, which may mean given relief, or squeezed by clouds; Ibn al-Mustanir takes it to mean rain.
rows.anchor: أي يؤتون بعصرة ويحتمل أن يكون من عصرات السحاب

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash records a reading that takes the word as squeezing moisture or similar liquid.
rows.anchor: وجعلها من عصر البلل ونحوه

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari strongly rejects deriving the word from refuge, but the author says he gives no proof.
rows.anchor: ورد الطبري على من جعل اللفظة من العصرة ردا كثيرا بغير حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage omits the messenger’s return and report; the king and courtiers admire Joseph’s interpretation and hearing of his truthfulness, increasing his standing.
rows.anchor: فرأى الملك وحاضروه نبل التعبير وحسن الرأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to learn the women’s case so the king will investigate whether his imprisonment was just; a small part of the story reveals the whole.
rows.anchor: يستقصي عن ذنبي وينظر في أمري، هل سجنت بحق أو بظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He avoids naming the governor’s wife out of good companionship and loyalty to her husband.
rows.anchor: ونكب عن ذكر امرأة العزيز حسن عشرة ورعاية لذمام ملك العزيز له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr from ʿAsim and Abu Ḥaywah read niswah with a ḍamma; others read it with a kasra, both accepted plural forms.
rows.anchor: وهما لغتان في تكسير نساء الذي هو اسم جمع لا واحد له من لفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers vary between the plural forms اللايي and اللاتي, both derived from التي.
rows.anchor: بالياء، وقرأ فرقة «اللاتي» بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph delays release to secure a public finding of innocence, fearing people would otherwise keep seeing him as the man who pursued his master’s wife.
rows.anchor: فأراد يوسف عليه السلام أن تبين براءته وتتحقق منزلته من العفة والخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report praises Joseph’s patience and gentleness and says the Prophet would have answered the call sooner; a route through Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim appears in Bukhari’s tafsir.
rows.anchor: ولو لبثت في السجن لبثه لأجبت الداعي ولم ألتمس العذر حينئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s statement is praise for Joseph; the Prophet describes a different but also sound judgment, accepting an earlier release and explaining himself afterward.
rows.anchor: لو كنت أنا لبادرت بالخروج ثم حاولت بيان عذري بعد ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These stories guide people facing future trials: delaying a chance to leave prison can lead to indefinite confinement, while Joseph knew by revelation he was safe.
rows.anchor: حالة حزم ومدح، وما فعله يوسف عليه السلام صبر عظيم وجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If رب means God, Joseph’s statement that He knows their plotting is a warning and threat.
rows.anchor: الله عز وجل، وفي الآية وعيد- على هذا- وتهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If رب means his master the governor, Joseph appeals to him and rebukes him; the pronoun in كيدهن refers to the named women in this investigation, not women generally.
rows.anchor: العزيز مولاه، ففي ذلك استشهاد به وتقريع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king assembles the women with the governor’s wife and asks what their affair was when they pursued Joseph.
rows.anchor: وامرأة العزيز معهن، وقال لهن: ما خطبكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women’s answer protects their own position and gives Joseph some vindication, but ما علمنا عليه من سوء is not a complete declaration of his innocence.
rows.anchor: ليس بإبراء تام، وإنما كان الإبراء التام وصف القصة على وجهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying they knew only good about Joseph would have been a stronger exoneration.
rows.anchor: ما علمن عليه إلا خيرا لكان أدخل في التبرية

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Bukhari classifies this kind of statement as testimony to a person’s reliability, citing Usama ibn Zayd’s statement in the slander report.
rows.anchor: وقد بوب البخاري على هذه الألفاظ على أنها تزكية

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik does not accept such words as sufficient to certify a witness, because they do not establish his moral uprightness.
rows.anchor: في تزكية الشاهد، لأنه ليس بإثبات العدالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaṣḥaṣ al-ḥaqq means that the truth became clear after being hidden; another explanation derives it from the separation of one share from another.
rows.anchor: تبين بعد خفائه، كذا قال الخليل وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The governor’s wife admits that she pursued Joseph and fully clears him of blame.
rows.anchor: ثم أقرت على نفسها بالمراودة والتزمت الذنب وأبرأت يوسف البراءة التامة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: After the brothers describe their hardship, Joseph is moved and weeps as he begins to reveal himself.
rows.anchor: وارفض دمعه باكيا فشرع في كشف أمره إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the brothers did to Joseph and Benjamin refers to separating them in childhood, mistreating Joseph, and humiliating Benjamin, not Benjamin’s later affair.
rows.anchor: والتمرس بهما وإذاية بنيامين. بعد مغيب يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ignorance can mean ignorance of the sin or the immaturity and lack of experience of youth; Joseph’s face and manner likely made them suspect who he was.
rows.anchor: وإما إلى جهل الشباب وقلة الحنكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers vary in the interrogative hamzas in أإنك; other forms insert an alif or ease the second hamza.
rows.anchor: بتحقيق الهمزتين، وقرأت فرقة بإدخال ألف بين همزتين

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن وقتادة وابن كثير
rows.claim: These readers use the declarative إنك, though some understand it as a question with the interrogative particle omitted.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن وقتادة وابن كثير «إنك»

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubay’s reading asks whether he is Joseph or whether the other brother is Joseph; Abu al-Fatḥ explains an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: أن في قراءة أبي بن كعب: «أو أنت يوسف»

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets piety as avoiding sin and patience as enduring prison.
rows.anchor: من يتق في ترك المعصية ويصبر في السجن

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi reads piety as abstaining from fornication and patience as remaining celibate.
rows.anchor: من يتق الزنى ويصبر على العزوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse intends a general principle covering major trials; the interpreters specify Joseph’s own experiences because those were his circumstances.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال هذان ما خصصا، لأنها كانت من نوازله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers omit the final yāʾ in يَتَّق, while Ibn Kathir retains it; several grammatical explanations are offered.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وحده: «من يتقي ويصبر» بإثبات الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation treats the yāʾ as vocalized and the jussive as loss of its vowel, but Abu ʿAli rejects this as a poetic rather than spoken construction.
rows.anchor: وهذا مما لا نحمله عليه، لأنه يجيء في الشعر لا في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations make من mean الذي with يتقي indicative and يَصبر coordinated by meaning, or treat يَصبر as raised but with a shortened final vowel.
rows.anchor: فعل مرفوع، و «يصبر» عطف على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ confession that God preferred Joseph is a plea for reconciliation and implicitly admits their guilt; athara covers all forms of preference and gifts.
rows.anchor: هذا منهم استنزال ليوسف وإقرار بالذنب في ضمنه استغفار منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāṭiʾūn means those who intentionally commit error, unlike mukhṭiʾ, one who aims correctly but misses; Umayya ibn al-Askar supplies a poetic example.
rows.anchor: وهو المعتمد للخطأ، والمخطئ من أخطأ، وهو الذي قصد الصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā tathrība ʿalaykum is a gracious pardon; Ikrima reports that God said Joseph’s forgiveness raised his renown.
rows.anchor: بعفوك على إخوتك رفعت لك ذكرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Ali advised Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya to appeal to the Prophet with the brothers’ words; the Prophet then answered, no reproach upon you.
rows.anchor: الرأي أن تلقيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tathrīb means blame, punishment, or related reproach; the Prophet’s instruction about a punished enslaved woman uses it in the sense of taunting.
rows.anchor: اللوم والعقوبة وما جرى معهما من سوء معتقد ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ where to pause: some after عليكم, while most pause after اليوم and take يغفر الله لكم as a supplication, as Ibn Ishaq and al-Tabari do.
rows.anchor: اليوم وابتدأ يغفر الله لكم على جهة الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pausing after اليوم is stronger because otherwise the verse asserts that God has forgiven them, unless that assertion came by revelation.
rows.anchor: لأن الآخر فيه حكم على مغفرة الله، اللهم إلا أن يكون ذلك بوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s assurance that the shirt will restore his father’s sight shows that this instruction came through revelation.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن هذا كله بوحي وإعلام من الله

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash reports that the shirt belonged to Abraham, came from Paradise when he left the fire, then passed to Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph.
rows.anchor: وروي أن هذا القميص كان لإبراهيم كساه الله إياه حين خرج من النار وكان من ثياب الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this account needs a chain of transmission; the apparent reading is that it was Joseph’s ordinary shirt, which makes its scent detectable at a distance unsurprising.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه قميص يوسف الذي هو منه بمنزلة قميص كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports give the arriving family as eighty people or seventy-six; their descendants later left Egypt with Moses in six hundred thousand.
rows.anchor: ثمانين نسمة، وقيل ستة وسبعين نفسا بين رجال ونساء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says that after revealing himself, Joseph asked about his father and learned he had gone blind from weeping, so Joseph sent the shirt.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: ذهب بصره من البكاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s home is identified either near Jerusalem or in al-Jazira; the author prefers near Jerusalem because their traces and graves are there.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان بالجزيرة والأول أصح لأن آثارهم وقبورهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph’s scent reached Jacob across an eight-day journey when a wind carried it.
rows.anchor: مسيرة ثمانية أيام، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj give the distance as eighty farsakhs; Ibn Jurayj says Joseph had been gone for seventy-seven years.
rows.anchor: قاله الحسن- وابن جريج قال: وقد كان فارقه قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Another report from al-Hasan gives the distance as a thirty-day journey; the author considers this close to Ibn Abbas’s account.
rows.anchor: مسيرة ثلاثين يوما، قاله الحسن بن أبي الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو أيوب الهوزني
rows.claim: Abu Ayyub al-Hawzani reports that the wind asked permission to carry Joseph’s scent to Jacob and was permitted.
rows.anchor: أن الريح استأذنت في أن توصل عرف يوسف إلى يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob addressed people around him who were variously said to be his grandchildren, some of his sons, or relatives.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا بعض بنيه، وقيل: كانوا قرابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tufannidūn means to reject Jacob’s judgment or argue back; afsada al-dahr means that time ruined someone.
rows.anchor: تردون رأيي وتدفعون في صدري، وهذا هو التفنيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poets use fanad for ruin and decay; al-Mundhir ibn Saʿid says a man can be described as an old fool but not a woman.
rows.anchor: شيخ مفند: أي قد فسد رأيه، ولا يقال: عجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may accuse someone of fanad because of ignorance, overpowering desire, lying, or weakness and mental decline.
rows.anchor: يقع إما لجهل المفند، وإما لهوى غلبه، وإما لكذبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada say the brothers meant that Jacob was foolish; Ibn Abbas also glosses it as ignorance.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة: معناه تسفهون

rows.speaker: ابن جبير وعطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr and ʿAtaʾ interpret the phrase as accusing Jacob of lying.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير وعطاء: معناه: تكذبون

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the brothers meant that Jacob had become weak.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: معناه: تضعفون

rows.speaker: ابن زيد ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and Mujahid say the brothers meant to accuse Jacob of having lost his mind.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد ومجاهد: معناه: تقولون: ذهب عقلك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the phrase as saying that Jacob had grown old.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه: تهرمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author thinks the brothers accused Jacob because they believed his love for Joseph had overpowered his judgment.
rows.anchor: والذي يشبه أن تفنيدهم ليعقوب إنما كان لأنهم كانوا يعتقدون أن هواه قد غلبه في جانب يوسف

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says the root sense of fanad is corruption.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: أصل التفنيد الإفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers’ phrase your old error means Jacob’s persistent fixation and bewilderment, not religious misguidance; Qatada says their words were harsh and improper toward a father and prophet.
rows.anchor: وليس هو بالضلال الذي هو في العرف ضد الرشاد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets their words as meaning Jacob’s mistake.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المعنى: لفي خطئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob’s grief had been renewed by Benjamin’s situation, earning him the description ذو الحزنين, the man of two sorrows.
rows.anchor: وكان حزن يعقوب قد تجدد بقصة بنيامين، فلذلك يقال له: ذو الحزنين

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Some take أو as إِلّا أن, as in Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse about trying to gain a kingdom or dying.
rows.anchor: أو هنا بمعنى: «إلا أن» كما هي في قول امرئ القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the ordinary either-or sense here because the unbelievers force the messengers to choose one of two outcomes; he says the poem requires the sense unless, since death was not their aim.
rows.anchor: وتحمل أو في هذه الآية أن تكون على بابها لوقوع أحد الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation of أو as حتى is weak here; constructions that are often paraphrased that way can instead be understood as إلا أن.
rows.anchor: هي بمعنى «حتى» في الآية، وهذا ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return normally means returning to a former condition, but the messengers had never been unbelievers; the threat therefore means returning to silence and anonymity, which the unbelievers count as joining their religion.
rows.anchor: إلى حالة قد كانت، والرسل ما كانوا قط في ملة الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God singles out the wrongdoers for destruction because some of those who made the threat might yet believe.
rows.anchor: وخصص تعالى الظالمين من الذين كفروا إذ جائز أن يؤمن من الكفرة الذين قالوا المقالة ناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address promises the present audience and their descendants the land, just as postponement to an appointed term can include descendants.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للحاضرين، والمراد هم وذريتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ḥaywah reads both verbs about destruction and settling with a yāʾ instead of the expected nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: «ليهلكن» و «ليسكننكم» بالياء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqāmī can mean God’s act of standing over creation in power or the servant’s standing before Him for judgment in the afterlife; the different possessive relations are all idiomatic.
rows.anchor: بالقدرة، ويحتمل أن يريد به الظرف لقيام العبد بين يديه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The liquid is not actually water, but is called water because it takes water’s place; ṣadīd means pus and blood flowing from the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: ليس بماء لكن لما كان بدل الماء في العرف عندنا عد ماء

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak gloss ṣadīd as pus and blood.
rows.anchor: ما يسيل من أجساد أهل النار، قاله مجاهد والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of swallowing it and barely getting it down conveys how difficult the drink is to bear.
rows.anchor: يتجرعه ولا يكاد يسيغه عبارة عن صعوبة أمره عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report depicts the drink scorching the face and making the scalp fall before it cuts the drinker’s intestines.
rows.anchor: فإذا أدنيت منه شوت وجهه وسقطت فيها فروة رأسه فإذا شربها قطعت أمعاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death approaches the condemned from every hair on his body, according to Ibrahim al-Taymi, or from all six directions; he is not released by dying.
rows.anchor: أي من كل شعرة في بدنه، قاله إبراهيم التيمي، وقيل من جميع جهاته الست

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ explains the severe punishment as holding breath inside the bodies.
rows.anchor: العذاب الغليظ حبس الأنفاس في الأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final pronoun in مِن ورائه can refer back to the preceding punishment.
rows.anchor: إن الضمير في ورائه هنا هو للعذاب المتقدم

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh supplies an introductory phrase such as what is recited or told to you before مثل الذين كفروا.
rows.anchor: أن التقدير: فيما يتلى عليكم أو يقص: مثل الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and al-Farra make مثل the subject and كرماد its predicate, with the sense that the unbelievers’ works are like ash.
rows.anchor: أنه ابتداء خبره كرماد والتقدير عندهم: مثل أعمال الذين كفروا كرماد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra also reportedly allows مثل to be redundant, yielding the direct sense that the unbelievers’ works are ash.
rows.anchor: أنه يرى إلغاء مثل وأن المعنى: الذين كفروا أعمالهم كرماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers treating مثل and أعمالهم as successive subjects, with the whole sentence Works are like ash as the predicate of the first.
rows.anchor: المتحصل مثالا في النفس للذين كفروا هذه الجملة المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The works of unbelievers vanish when needed like ash blown away by fierce wind, leaving no trace or recoverable gain.
rows.anchor: وشبهت أعمال الكفرة ومساعيهم في فسادها وقت الحاجة وتلاشيها بالرماد الذي تذروه الريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is called ʿāṣif though the wind is literally what blows fiercely; the description extends from wind to the day in which it occurs.
rows.anchor: وهي من صفة الريح بالحقيقة- لما كانت في اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafiʿ and Abu Jaʿfar read الرياح in the plural; the other readers use the singular الريح.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وحده وأبو جعفر «الرياح» والباقون «الريح» بالإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points to the unbelievers’ condition and their deep misguidance, far from the clear road to salvation.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى كونهم بهذه الحال، وعلى مثل هذا الغرور، والضلال البعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Sulami reads يوم عاصف in an annexed construction; he also reports a reading of ألم تر with a silent rāʾ meaning do you not know.
rows.anchor: بسكون الراء، بمعنى ألم تعلم من رؤية القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use خلق as a past verb, while Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read خالق as an active participle, parallel to other divine creation titles.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «خالق السماوات»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating the heavens and earth in truth means creating them fittingly, for the welfare of servants, according to the prior decree, and as evidence of God’s power.
rows.anchor: ومن جهة مصالح عباده، وإنفاذ سابق قضائه، ولتدل عليه وعلى قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that God may remove people means He can annihilate them and erase their traces.
rows.anchor: أي يعدمكم ويطمس آثاركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A new creation could mean a different group of Adam’s descendants or another kind of creation; nothing of this is impossible for God.
rows.anchor: من فرق بني آدم، ويصح غير ذلك

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Some interpreters take mathal to mean description: the unbelievers have the worst description and God the highest description.
rows.anchor: أي لهؤلاء صفة السوء ولله الوصف الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this is unnecessary and departs from the wording; the literal likeness compares God’s alleged daughters to a human father of daughters, a hated likeness among the idolaters.
rows.anchor: لأنه خروج عن اللفظ، بل قوله مثل على بابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because idolaters themselves treat daughters as vile, God assigns them the likeness of every vile outcome, culminating in Hell.
rows.anchor: ليس في البنات فقط، لكن لما جعلوه هم في البنات جعله هو لهم على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s highest likeness denotes His self-sufficient perfection.
rows.anchor: وقوله ولله المثل الأعلى على الإطلاق أيضا في الكمال المستغني

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the highest likeness as the declaration that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: المثل الأعلى لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuʾākhidh is a reciprocal form of أخذ; the form can be understood as taking in response to sin or harm, with either of two verbal patterns.
rows.anchor: هو تفاعل من أخذ، كأن أحد المتؤاخذين يأخذ من الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun عليها refers to the earth, though earth has not been named, because it is familiar and can be indicated without prior mention, as in the poem about the sun.
rows.anchor: عائد على الأرض، وتمكن ذلك مع أنه لم يجر لها ذكر لشهرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The مِن in مِن دابة covers every kind of creature; the passage begins to explain that immediate punishment for deserved sin would leave no creature alive.
rows.anchor: دخلت من لاستغراق الجنس، وظاهر الآية أن الله تعالى أخبر أنه لو أخذ الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls earlier peoples as a warning to the present audience and comfort to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: هذه آية ضرب مثل لهم بمن تقدم وفي ضمنها وعيد لهم وتأنيس للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Today may mean the day of revelation, when the earlier peoples had died and Satan alone remained their ally, or the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: وهو بعد موت أولئك الأمم المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Today may instead refer to their lifetime, expressed as today to make the former peoples’ lifespan a warning to present listeners.
rows.anchor: مدة حياتهم، ثم انقطعت ولايته بموتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Qur’an; the purpose phrase means it was sent for clarification, guidance, and mercy.
rows.anchor: يريد القرآن، وقوله لتبين لهم في موضع المفعول من أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement includes every form of disbelief, but here the focus is denial of God’s lordship and assigning divinity to idols, as the following signs establish.
rows.anchor: ولكن الإشارة في هذه الآية إنما هي لجحدهم الربوبية وتشريكهم الأصنام في الألوهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain and the revival of the earth are clear evidence for God’s lordship; the dead and living earth are metaphors for barren and growing land.
rows.anchor: التي هي أبين العبر، وهي ملاك الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to those who hear suits an evident sign that requires only listening, not deep reflection.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يحتاج إلى تفكر ولا نظر قلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anʿām comprises camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; ʿibra is the state from which one draws a lesson.
rows.anchor: الأصناف الأربعة: الإبل والبقر والضأن والمعز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ on whether نسقيكم begins with a fatḥa from saqā or a ḍamma from asqā; some lexicographers call the verbs synonymous, while others distinguish single versus repeated watering.
rows.anchor: هما لغتان بمعنى واحد، وقالت فرقة: تقول لمن تسقيه بالشفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Raja reads يسقيكم with a yāʾ, meaning God gives you drink; another group reads تسقيكم with a feminine tāʾ, a weak reading also discussed in Sura al-Muʾminun.
rows.anchor: أي يسقيكم الله، وقرأت فرقة «تسقيكم» بالتاء وهي ضعيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in مما في بطونه can refer to the animal kind as a collective or to anʿām understood as the singular naʿam.
rows.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: مثل الفراخ نتفت حواصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the pronoun as referring to some animals, since males do not produce milk.
rows.anchor: الضمير عائد على البعض، إذ الذكور لا ألبان لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farth is material that descends into the intestines; sāʾigh means easy and pleasant to drink.
rows.anchor: ما ينزل إلى الأمعاء، و «السائغ» السهل في الشرب اللذيذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One group reads siyghan with a doubled yāʾ, while ʿIsa al-Thaqafi reads it with a silent yāʾ as a lightened form; the root is wāw-based, from sawagha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى الثقفي «سيغا» بسكون الياء وهي تخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says milk has never choked anyone, and another attributes this statement to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لم يشرق به أحد قط، وروي ذلك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari supplies an omitted relative clause: from the fruits are things that you take.
rows.anchor: التقدير ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب ما تتخذون

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group supplies an omitted word meaning some or a thing that you take from the fruits.
rows.anchor: التقدير ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب شيء تتخذون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may coordinate with livestock as another sign and blessing, or with the previous مِن phrase as another drink made from fruit.
rows.anchor: عطفا على الأنعام [النحل: 66] أي ولكم من ثمرات النخيل والأنعام عبرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this verse preceded the prohibition of wine: السكر means wine and good provision means lawful food and drink from dates and grapes.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية قبل تحريم الخمر، وأراد بالسكر الخمر

rows.speaker: ابن جبير وإبراهيم والشعبي وأبو زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim, al-Shaʿbi, and Abu Zayd share the reading that السكر is wine before the prohibition and good provision is other lawful food and drink.
rows.anchor: وقال بهذا القول ابن جبير وإبراهيم والشعبي وأبو زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God mentioned the blessing of intoxicating drink before wine was prohibited.
rows.anchor: ذكر الله نعمته في السكر قبل تحريم الخمر

rows.speaker: الشعبي ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi and Mujahid take sugar to mean a wholesome, non-intoxicating drink such as vinegar, syrup, or nabīdh; good provision means dates and grapes.
rows.anchor: السكر السائغ من هاتين الشجرتين كالخل والرب والنبيذ

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says sugar can mean food in Arabic and prefers that reading, which includes no wine and requires no abrogation.
rows.anchor: ما يطعم، ورجح الطبري هذا القول، ولا مدخل للخمر فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some who identify sugar as wine say the verse was abrogated by the wine prohibition, but the author calls this flawed because abrogation concerns an established legal ruling.
rows.anchor: لأن النسخ إنما يكون في حكم مستقر مشروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound prophetic report says wine itself is prohibited and so is anything else intoxicating; Iraqis transmitted a different vocalization associated with their rule allowing small amounts of other drinks.
rows.anchor: هكذا في الرواية الصحيحة بفتح السين والكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḥy in Arabic is a hidden conveyance of meaning; here it is inspiration rather than prophetic revelation, as interpreters agree, though the word can also mean command.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى بأن ربك أوحى لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads إلى النخل with a fatḥa on the ḥāʾ; أن introduces an explanation of the inspiration.
rows.anchor: بفتح الحاء وأن في قوله أن اتخذي مفسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made bee homes in mountain crevices, hollow trees, and human-made structures such as hives and walls.
rows.anchor: إما في الجبال وكواها، وإما في متجوف الأشجار، وإما فيما يعرش ابن آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿArsh means to prepare or arrange, especially branches and wood into a crafted, shaded structure; the term is used for the shelter made for the Prophet at Badr.
rows.anchor: معناه هيأ، وأكثر ما يستعمل فيما يكون من إتقان الأغصان والخشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yaʿrishūn is read with either kasra or ḍamma; Ibn Zayd says it means vines, while al-Tabari says roofs, and the author finds both explanations imprecise.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد في قوله: يعرشون قال الكروم، وقال الطبري ومما يعرشون يعني ما يبنون من السقوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to eat is inspired after the command to make homes; مِن is partitive because bees eat only some flowers from all fruits.
rows.anchor: أن كلي، فعطف كلي على اتخذي، ومن للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subl means routes of flight and travel; they belong to the Lord because He created and enabled them.
rows.anchor: من حيث هي ملكه وخلقه التي يسر لك ربك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes ذللا as an adjective of the bees: obedient and guided along their way.
rows.anchor: أي مطيعة منقادة لما يسرت له، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says people go out for forage and the bees follow them.
rows.anchor: فهم يخرجون بالنحل ينتجعون وهي تتبعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively ذللا describes the paths as smooth and straight; Mujahid says the bee encounters no rough path.
rows.anchor: لا يتوعر عليها سبيل تسلكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taming of bees recalls the Qur’anic description of livestock made manageable for people.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما فهم لها مالكون وذللناها لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people say honey comes out of bees’ mouths, though an account attributed to Ali’s remarks about worldly goods suggests it comes from elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وجمهور الناس على أن العسل يخرج من أفواه النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honey’s colors and flavors vary with different bees and sources of forage; Zaynab described the bees’ forage to explain a smell like maghafir.
rows.anchor: في العسل بحسب اختلاف النحل والمراعي وقد يختلف طعمه بحسب اختلاف المراعي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The pronoun in فيه شفاء refers to honey, but the statement promises healing in some cases and conditions, as with other medicines, not every disease in every person.
rows.anchor: ولا يقتضي العموم في كل علة وفي كل إنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse highlights honey as a medicine that often heals and is used alongside other remedies in drinks and compounds.
rows.anchor: ففائدة الآية إخبار منبه منه في أنه دواء كما كثر الشفاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reportedly treated every complaint with honey, including applying it to boils while reciting the verse.
rows.anchor: إلا تداوى بالعسل، حتى إنه كان يدهن به الدمل والضرحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umar’s practice implies that he considered honey healing in all cases.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أنه يرى الشفاء به على العموم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the pronoun in فيه شفاء refers to the Qur’an, which contains healing.
rows.anchor: الضمير للقرآن، أي فيه شفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author ridicules an esoteric claim that bees represent the Prophet’s family and honey represents the Qur’an and wisdom.
rows.anchor: وذهب قوم من أهل الجهالة إلى أن هذه الآية إنما يراد بها أهل البيت ورجال بني هاشم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At al-Mansur’s gathering, a man mocked that interpretation by asking that the ruler’s food and drink come from the bellies of Hashemites, exposing its absurdity.
rows.anchor: جعل الله طعامك وشرابك مما يخرج من بطون بني هاشم، فأضحك الحاضرين
